origin_result.basis: The origin check could not be completed because the required information was not provided. The product-specific rule requires both a tariff shift (CTSH) and at least 45% value addition on an FOB basis, or 40% on an Ex-Works basis. No checks could be performed because a bill of materials and a declaration were not provided.

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory. The factory must be located outside a free zone, hold a MoIAT industrial licence, and have a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added. Registration takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The issuing authority requires the certificate application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product. Each item must qualify separately in its own right. The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and conducting a factory visit.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade issues the certificate through the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service. Log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the service, and fill in the application form.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade requires proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice to be uploaded.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee. The fee range is AED 10 to AED 200, depending on the invoice value in AED.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade processes the application in about one working day. Submit the application and receive approval, or a return with comments to correct.

The competent authority issues the certificate prior to, at or within five working days of the date of exportation. The certificate is valid for twelve months from the date of issue and for only one import. It shall bear the authorised signature and official seal of the competent authority. A certificate may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 of India's certificate form.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, including which origin criterion is claimed. The importer keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing and must answer a customs request within 10 working days.

The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for no less than five years, starting from the end of the year of the date of its issue. Any failure to consent to a verification visit shall be grounds for a denial of preferential benefits.

The exporter ships the goods directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If a third party issues the invoice, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

caveats.note: The '+' in the origin rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

The processing 'cut and assembled from imported aluminium profiles' may involve simple cutting and simple assembly, which are minimal operations that never confer origin under the agreement, whatever the product-specific rule says.
The agreement says box 8 for retrospective issuance remarks, but India's certificate form says box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a 3-year record-keeping minimum, but the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit, but this is unconfirmed (seen only in secondary sources).

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
De minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the value-addition percentage.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating. The last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.
Indirect materials (such as fuel, tools and consumables used in production) count as neither originating nor non-originating.
